# Phase 4J9 — registered PCFF profiles and final polymer graphs

Base: `633d6d5ede69dcddea9d550edcdec0adb93d6f4c` (merged J8).
Branch: `codex/phase-4j9-pcff-profile-registry`. No merge or main changes.

## Runtime architecture

The runtime input is the final `MolecularSystem` constructed from PSMILES. Native
PCFF perception, oriented bond increments, Class II assignment, model assembly,
evaluation, minimization, bundles and workflows do not consume CAR/MDF files or
invoke msi2lmp. Coordinates are generated by the construction adapter; assignment
uses chemical topology rather than coordinates, repeat names or isolated-repeat
charge copying.

`build_polymer_from_sequence` supports explicit sequences; the existing linear,
alternating, block and random builders retain their behavior. Optional
`head_end_group`/`tail_end_group` are one-dummy, single-bond SMILES on the sequence
and homopolymer builders. Default hydrogen termination and historical metadata
are unchanged. Explicit ends preserve source atom indices and head/tail roles.
They currently require ETKDG or 2D construction; local-template placement for
arbitrary ends is explicitly rejected. Existing homopolymer tacticity support is
preserved; mixed-sequence tacticity remains restricted by the existing builder.
No chemistry, stereochemistry, isotope, radical or mass is silently changed to
fit a PCFF profile.

`edit_polymer_topology` copies a system, removes explicitly named hydrogens and
adds explicitly named single crosslink bonds. It preserves surviving IDs,
coordinates and metadata and records the edit. This is not automated curing.
`reassign_pcff_polymer` validates the previous preparation, computes changed sites
and neighboring environments, locally retypes them in global ring/component
context, and compares them against the fully validated final typing. Validated
source/type lookup results can be reused only with identical source and policy.
All interaction inventories, shortest-path pairs and equilibrium dependencies are
rebuilt. Native integrity validation independently resolves the new candidate.
Stale assignments cannot bind to the edited graph. Full validation is deliberately
retained; this API makes no performance or minimal-neighborhood guarantee.

Repeat, chain, inter-repeat, terminal and crosslink roles are retained in owned
`PCFFFinalGraphPreparation` evidence and the original bundle system. The evidence
contains native ordered interaction selections and site provenance; chemical
fingerprints remain independent of coordinate-generation or repeat annotations.

## Registry and authorization

`list_pcff_profiles`, `inspect_pcff_profile`, `select_pcff_profile` and
`validate_pcff_profile_system` operate offline. Registrations are code-owned and
versioned, with `candidate`, `audited`, `operational` or `unsupported` states.
`save_pcff_profile_registration`/`load_pcff_profile_registration` validate the whole
registration against that authority. Editing JSON and recomputing a checksum does
not promote a source or change its graph domain.

Operational profiles:

- `island_pcff_benzenoid_c6h6_v1`: J8's exact payload, graph scope and identity
  `db14223b8527ca7d4f9cafb3cca2b40610ff6c944cde18108ffa46dcbb38228d` are preserved.
- `island_pcff_linked_benzenoid_polymer_v1`: connected, neutral explicit-H graphs
  composed of six-carbon aromatic cycles connected by single bonds, with optional
  methyl ends/substituents. This includes final phenylene sequences, branching and
  explicitly edited links whose required source rows are complete. Fused rings,
  heteroatoms, charged/isotopic/radical states, assigned stereocenters and other
  aliphatic environments are not authorized. The graph predicate is necessary but
  insufficient: native charge, source selection and every active term must pass.

The full pinned catalog is `audited`, not operational. PCFF-IFF v1.5 and LUNAR
PCFF-IFF v1.6 are `candidate`, with no runtime capabilities. Pyridinium and
printed-residual guanidinium registrations are `unsupported`. All registrations
retain conservative readiness flags. Legacy unprofiled native preparations remain
readable and behaviorally unchanged; explicit registry-selected preparation can
execute only an operational entry.

The new profile uses the existing source-graph v1 typing, native increments and
Class II interpretation. It adds authorization and final-graph evidence rather
than new equations or atom rules. `prepare_pcff_polymer(..., mode="strict")`
requires a selected operational profile, complete raw source assignments, and
source-row provenance for every active term. Missing rows, ambiguous records and
policy-derived zeros cannot yield a strict preparation. Explicit source zeros are
valid. `mode="diagnostic"` returns a ledger and never a prepared result, even if
its observed model happens to be complete.

## Optional interoperability

`export_msi2lmp_car_mdf(system, output_dir, types=..., charges=..., provenance=...)`
returns an owned round-tripped system after exclusive candidate publication.
It writes CAR, MDF, a typed data-only sidecar and checksums. Coordinates retain
17-digit float precision; MDF connections include bond order. The reversible
index/name/stable-ID map and all chemical/polymer metadata remain in the required
sidecar. CAR/MDF alone cannot losslessly represent all ISLAND state and are not
accepted as native input. `load_msi2lmp_car_mdf` checks physical files against the
sidecar, including after an attacker recomputes checksums. Changing coordinates,
connectivity, labels or charges in only one representation is rejected. Export
neither infers nor certifies supplied types/charges and never invokes a converter.

msi2lmp supplies a bounded independent conversion control only. Its input atom
types are external; it does not establish automatic typing or bond-increment
correctness and lacks auto-equivalence supplementation. No `-ignore` is used.
The retained H5 angle-angle equilibrium-role correction remains separately
recorded and reconstructed from the reference's own angle inventory. Existing
wildcard reversal ambiguities and nonzero Wilson-equilibrium limitations remain.

## Declared acceptance and reproducible commands

Declarations precede production implementation:
`phase_4j9_audit_declaration.json` preserves the preliminary toluene audit;
`phase_4j9_polymer_declaration.json` redirects the product slice to final PSMILES
polymer graphs. `phase_4j9_vertical_declaration.json` fixes the DP2 input checksum,
reference executables, seeds, tolerances and budgets. No failed input is replaced.

External artifact root: `../island-validation/phase4j9-declared`.
Primary Python: `../island-validation/phase4e2-env/bin/python`.
FRC: `../island-validation/phase4h1-sources/lammps/pcff.frc`.

```sh
python -m island.forcefields.pcff.registry_cli
python examples/pcff_psmiles_profile.py --source /verified/pcff.frc --dp 2
python scripts/inspect_pcff_polymer_profiles.py --source /verified/pcff.frc --output /new/polymer-matrix
python scripts/validate_pcff_registry.py --source /verified/pcff.frc --output /new/vertical-slice
python scripts/inspect_pcff_registry_sources.py --source /verified/pcff.frc --variants-declaration docs/evidence/phase_4j7_declaration.json --output /new/coverage.json --require-full-source
```

Use explicit local paths in the declarations for external source libraries and
validation executables. Runtime assignment needs neither LAMMPS nor msi2lmp.
Evaluation requires OpenMM; minimization additionally requires SciPy. PSMILES
construction needs RDKit. Data-only source, profile, bundle and workflow
inspection keep scientific backend imports lazy.

The DP2 reference independently reads raw FRC rows, selects charge increments and
parameters, and checks topology inventories before numerical evaluation. The
converter receives graph/types/charges, not ISLAND's compiled coefficients.
LAMMPS independently evaluates initial and asymmetric perturbed coordinates,
final verified minima, and retained workflow frames. FD displacements are
`1e-4`, `1e-5`, `1e-6` angstrom. Numerical tolerances are unchanged:
energy and forces `atol=1e-5`, `rtol=2e-10` in canonical kJ/mol and
kJ/(mol*angstrom); coefficient/charge `1e-12`; split continuation `atol=1e-10`,
`rtol=1e-12`. Minimization is bounded at 5000 iterations/10000 evaluations with
maximum atomic force tolerance 0.1. BAOAB is four steps, two per segment, with
300 K, friction 5/ps, 0.1 fs, velocity seed 78123 and thermostat seed 99181.

## Coverage and remaining gates

The machine-readable source ledger separates row inventory, ordinary and automatic
equivalences, typing, charges, lower-order/cross-term assignment, executable
interpretation, independent verification, registry authorization and final polymer
coverage. All 133 native labels remain visible; 86 have existing predicates and
47 remain unresolved. J9 adds no generic chemical fallback and no global type
completion. Candidate inventories retain every label separately (214/240) with
runtime status unauthorized. A bounded polymer observation does not certify all
environments of cp, hc or c3.

Exact remaining work includes nh+ increments; guanidinium's printed 0.9999 e
component total; sulfur/lactam missing or ambiguous couplings; na–hn2 coverage;
unresolved wildcard reversal precedence; nonzero Wilson signed/permutation
semantics; domain-specific charged/metal/zeolite typing and charge conventions;
and source-empty torsion-torsion scope. The ledger retains individual source rows,
equivalences and next actions. None is converted to zero, normalized, renamed or
filled from another force field.

The full-source command remains nonzero. Graph shape support and polymer-role
preservation do not imply general chemical support, periodic capability, network
curing, equilibration or scientific accuracy. `production_validated=False` and
`simulation_readiness="not_established"` remain unchanged.

### Actual polymer acceptance

All nine declared final graphs passed strict typing, native charges, complete raw
source-backed assignments and executable model construction. Independently
selected raw-source records, original/native charge vectors, and topology
inventories agree. All nine passed LAMMPS comparisons at retained and asymmetric
perturbed coordinates: maximum grouped energy error `3.725290298461914e-8` kJ/mol;
maximum force-component error `1.5903434163466734e-6` kJ/(mol*angstrom). The larger
energy discrepancy is in the unrelaxed crosslinked geometry; it passed the
predeclared absolute/relative test without altered inputs or tolerances.

The principal DP2 slice uses model identity
`dc6f60273e070cfe32ffb6568087ee43a3a5d19aad74570492b0bbc8c13ad9fb`,
profile identity `bfd950ed34c26e87aada95232a74616255e82b3faa0f501876b5874f6209b4a0`,
and facade identity `e40553c7664d431e0208b0de3192d5dacc7775fcb5358f7847711fd45e06e5de`.
It minimized in **78 iterations, 83 actual evaluations**, from
536.144955544251 to 506.03072523648075 kJ/mol. Maximum/RMS forces were
0.07660584226766147 / 0.04374344769618155 kJ/(mol*angstrom); independent fresh
verification passed. FD errors at successively smaller displacements were
`3.84298e-5`, `3.84472e-7`, `1.37385e-7` kJ/(mol*angstrom).

The four-step BAOAB workflow relocated both bundle and run directory and resumed
in child PID 747042. All common frame differences were measured zero; complete
RNG state and original trajectory identity match exactly. This is same-host
continuation consistency. Startup used five Contexts (two for minimization and
three for the first segment), uninterrupted dynamics three, and child resume
three. Dynamics evaluation consumption was six uninterrupted versus eight
across two segments, including independent segment boundaries. Five synchronized
frames were retained. Completed status, frame reading and no-op resume passed,
including offline inspection with scientific imports blocked. No setup was
repeated during resume.

The additional whole-graph numerical command is:

```sh
python scripts/validate_pcff_polymer_graphs.py --source /verified/pcff.frc --matrix /retained/polymer-matrix --output /new/polymer-numerical
```

Its declaration captures all retained input hashes before evaluation. It loads
validated source assignments rather than rebuilding, retyping or preparing
inputs. The converter receives independently authored labels and raw-source
charges; it does not receive ISLAND-selected parameter coefficients. Tetrahedral
methyl Wilson exclusion is checked independently while every angle-angle request
is retained. Raw converter output and explicit H5 equilibrium-role overrides are
preserved separately.

These are new authorization, provenance and polymer-level verification gates;
the underlying cp/hc/c3 graph rules and equations already existed. General
source coverage is not increased by reclassifying queryable rows.

The unresolved predicate labels are:
`Ag Al Au Br Cl Cr Cu Fe K Li Mo Na Ni Pb Pd Pt Sn W az c_a ca+ cg ci cr h* h+ hb hi hoa hos n+ n1 n2 nb nho ni nz oah oas ob oe osh oss p= s- sf sz`.
Case and punctuation identify source types, not generic elements. See
`phase_4j9_gaps.json` for source lines, equivalence rows and interaction-specific
J6 blockers. An implemented label can still have missing native charges/couplings.

The optional exported real DP2 CAR/MDF package round-tripped original coordinates,
stable IDs, connectivity and all metadata exactly. Its separately executed
converter control completed without `-ignore`. An initial control invocation had
an incorrect relative executable path and is retained as an execution failure;
the corrected absolute-path command uses the same source and exported files.
It is not a retry of failed scientific parameterization.

End-group construction preserves tetrahedral atom chirality by explicitly
accounting for neighbor-order changes when the dummy is replaced. Unsupported
assigned bond stereochemistry is rejected before assembly because the current
core bond contract cannot represent it. No stereo metadata is silently removed.

A durable workflow uses the same prepared result, without interoperability files:

```python
from island.forcefields import PreparedForceFieldSources, save_prepared_forcefield
from island.workflows import PreparedWorkflowConfig, start_prepared_bundle_workflow

sources = PreparedForceFieldSources(pcff_frc=verified_frc_path)
final = prepare_pcff_polymer(final_system, options)
save_prepared_forcefield(final_system, final.prepared, bundle_dir, sources=sources)
status = start_prepared_bundle_workflow(
    bundle_dir, run_dir,
    PreparedWorkflowConfig(total_steps=4, segment_steps=2, recording_interval=1,
                           max_evaluations_per_segment=4, max_frames_per_segment=3),
    sources=sources,
)
```

After relocating the run, a separate process calls
`resume_prepared_workflow(relocated_run, sources=sources)` with the explicitly
resolved FRC. It loads the retained bundle, minimum, initialization and checkpoint;
it does not repeat construction, typing, native preparation or minimization.
The executable acceptance harness performs and verifies exactly this sequence.

The optional converter's own `.data` writer is not lossless: pinned
`WriteDataFile.c:391` uses `%15.9f` coordinates and `%9.6f` charges. A separate exact
converter-output equality check failed and is retained. Its measured coordinate
serialization difference is `4.993019331323012e-10` angstrom, with unchanged
charges and 23 bonds. The exported CAR/MDF/sidecar round-trip remains exact.
No acceptance tolerance was altered to relabel the failed exact check. The
independent numerical harness explicitly installs the declared coordinates in
LAMMPS using 17-digit `set atom` commands; raw converter output is retained.

These checks establish internal consistency and bounded implementation fidelity,
not authenticity of arbitrary caller-supplied scientific data.

Release verification: **1,642 passed, 10 skipped** in the final ordinary suite
(1656.33 seconds). The earlier full run passed 1,638/10 before the final additional
controls. Focused registry/historical workflow verification passed 74 tests;
final strict evidence checks passed 15, and the final three construction-boundary
controls passed separately. Ruff and primary/isolated environment `pip check`
both pass. The single-point example executed against the real source. Full-source
inspection exits 1 as required. Exact commands, logs and SHA256 receipts are in
`phase_4j9_verification.json`; all generated systems/models/bundles/checkpoints
